info.title: Proxy API
info.description: The Apideck Proxy API forwards a request to the API of a downstream connector through Apideck Unify and returns the downstream response. Apideck injects the credentials stored for the consumer in Vault, so the caller only supplies its Apideck API key and application ID, the consumer and service to use, and the downstream URL.

tags.name: Execute
tags.description: Execute enables pass-through requests to downstream APIs with automatic authentication injection from Vault credentials.

get.description:
Proxies a downstream GET request to a service and injects the necessary credentials into a request stored in Vault. This allows you to have an additional security layer and logging without needing to rely on Unify for normalization.
**Note**: Vault will proxy all data to the downstream URL and method/verb in the headers.
Send the `x-apideck-consumer-id`, `x-apideck-downstream-url` and, where needed, `x-apideck-service-id`, `x-apideck-unified-api`, `x-apideck-downstream-authorization`, `x-apideck-timeout` and `x-apideck-follow-redirects` headers through the `headers` map.

requestBody.description: Depending on the verb/method of the request this will contain the request body you want to POST/PATCH/PUT

ProxyRequestObject.description: JSON object forwarded as the request body

ProxyRequestString.description: Plain string forwarded as the request body

ProxyRequestBody.description: Request body forwarded to the downstream service. It can be a JSON object, a plain string, or an array of JSON objects

ProxyRequestObjectArray.description: Array of JSON objects forwarded as the request body

Unauthorized.description: Unauthorized. The Apideck API key or application ID is missing or invalid

error.description: Contains an explanation of the status_code as defined in HTTP/1.1 standard (RFC 7231)

message.description: A human-readable message providing more details about the error.

detail.description: Contains parameter or domain specific information related to the error and why it occurred.

message.description: Error message from downstream provider or network layer

credentials_expire_at_ms.description: Unix timestamp (milliseconds) when credentials will be deleted if not refreshed. Only present for non-recoverable errors (401, 400). Credentials are preserved indefinitely for recoverable/network errors.

retry_after_ms.description: Unix timestamp (milliseconds) when token refresh retry is allowed after cooldown period expires.

cooldown_remaining_ms.description: Milliseconds remaining in cooldown period before retry is allowed.

debug.description: Debug information including request/response details and OAuth timing metadata

ref.description: Link to documentation of error type

ProxyError.description: Proxy error. The request could not be forwarded, or the downstream service returned an error, which is indicated by the x-apideck-downstream-error header

schema.description: Indicates if the error returned in the body is from the downstream

Ok.description: Response of the downstream service to the proxied request, with its status code, headers and body. The body can be JSON (an object or an array), XML, plain text, CSV, binary content or empty, depending on the downstream service. When `x-apideck-follow-redirects` is `false` and the downstream response would redirect to a presigned URL, the body is a JSON object with `url` and `expires_at` instead

id.name: id
id.description: ID of the record you are acting upon.

x-apideck-app-id.name: x-apideck-app-id
x-apideck-app-id.description: The ID of your Unify application

x-apideck-consumer-id.name: x-apideck-consumer-id
x-apideck-consumer-id.description: ID of the consumer which you want to get or push data from

x-apideck-service-id.name: x-apideck-service-id
x-apideck-service-id.description: Provide the service id you want to call (e.g., pipedrive). Only needed when a consumer has activated multiple integrations for a Unified API.

x-apideck-unified-api.name: x-apideck-unified-api
x-apideck-unified-api.description: Specify which unified API to use for the connection lookup. Required for multi-API connectors (e.g., Workday) to ensure the correct credentials are used.

x-apideck-downstream-method.name: x-apideck-downstream-method
x-apideck-downstream-method.description: Downstream method. If not provided the upstream method will be inherited,

x-apideck-downstream-authorization.name: x-apideck-downstream-authorization
x-apideck-downstream-authorization.description: Downstream authorization header. This will skip the Vault token injection.

x-apideck-timeout.name: x-apideck-timeout
x-apideck-timeout.description: Override the default downstream request timeout in milliseconds. The default is 28000 (28 seconds).

x-apideck-follow-redirects.name: x-apideck-follow-redirects
x-apideck-follow-redirects.description: Set to `false` to opt out of the redirect to the presigned download URL. Instead of a `30x` response, you receive a `200` JSON body `{ url, expires_at }` containing the URL and its expiry, which you can fetch explicitly. Use this if your client automatically forwards the `Authorization` header onto redirects, since the downstream storage provider will reject that request. Any value other than `false` (or omitting the header) preserves the default redirect behavior.

raw.name: raw
raw.description: Include raw response. Mostly used for debugging purposes

apiKey.description:
To access our API, you need to sign up and obtain your unique API key. Each Unify application is assigned a single API key. You can locate your API key in the Configuration Settings section of your Apideck application. Additionally, your application’s application_id is available on the same page.

Authenticate your API requests by including your test or live secret API key in the request header.

- Bearer authorization header: `Authorization: Bearer "YOUR_API_KEY_HERE"`
- Application id header: `x-apideck-app-id: "YOUR_APP_ID_HERE"`

You should use the public keys on the SDKs and the secret keys to authenticate API requests.

**Do not share or include your secret API keys on client side code.** Your API keys carry significant privileges. Please ensure to keep them 100% secure and be sure to not share your secret API keys in areas that are publicly accessible like GitHub.

Learn how to set the Authorization header inside Postman https://learning.postman.com/docs/postman/sending-api-requests/authorization/#api-key

Go to Unify to grab your API KEY https://app.apideck.com/unify/api-keys
